Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8491-handrolled-empty-placeholders`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and never writes the assignee field.

**Dispatched because your own report says the class can be RETIRED COMPLETELY**, not merely reduced: a repo-wide grep found `ObjectGrid` (three sites) and `RelatedList` (objectui#8475) to be the **only** carriers. A class with exactly two carriers and a shared replacement already in hand is worth closing rather than tracking.

⇒ **fold objectui#8475 into this branch** and close both. Say so in the PR body and reference both cards.

## Decision frame

**Settled:** these sites should use the shared `EmptyValue` from `@object-ui/components` rather than a hand-rolled span. The accessibility gap decides it — the hand-rolled ones carry **no `aria-label`**, so an empty cell has no accessible name while its renderer-supplied neighbours do.

**Yours to measure:** whether `EmptyValue` is reachable from both call sites without a new dependency edge, and what the visual delta actually is (your report says the hand-rolled ones render **one size smaller and italic** — say whether adopting the shared one is a deliberate visual change or a no-op). **Measured cost is the whole basis.**

⚠️ **Verify the grep's completeness before trusting "only two carriers".** That claim is what justifies retiring the class, so it needs a census by **mechanism** — the em-dash character, the muted-foreground class pattern, and any `No value` string — each with a lit control, not one pattern. objectui#8394 found a fifth spelling its own census missed because the operands were reversed; objectui#8481 found three renderers where the card named one.

⚠️ Ask which of your cases an implementation that renders **`EmptyValue` everywhere, including for filled cells**, would still pass. A "the cell has an accessible name" assertion passes on that caricature. Pin a filled cell as the non-regression half.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8503 is out of draft and armed.

I re-measured the three load-bearing claims from `origin/main` independently, with a lit control on every instrument that could have returned zero. All three hold.

### 1. The fourth site the card missed — confirmed

On `origin/main` the carrier shape is exactly five sites in **two** files:

| site | spelling |
|---|---|
| `RelatedList.tsx:1007` | `text-xs italic` |
| `ObjectGrid.tsx:2479` / `:2497` / `:2697` | `text-xs italic` — the card's three |
| **`ObjectGrid.tsx:4362`** | **`text-sm italic` + `t('grid.empty')`** |

The fourth is invisible to the card's own instrument: grepping the `text-xs` string the card supplies cannot reach a `text-sm` spelling. On the branch all five are gone, and every remaining `muted-foreground/50` hit is a grip handle, a separator dot or a search icon — noise you excluded correctly.

**One correction.** Your instrument-2 line reads *"3 files, 5 sites"*. The carriers are 5 sites in **2** files; the diffstat agrees (two source files changed). If the third file in that count is `components/src/custom/empty.tsx` — the authority itself, correctly not a carrier — say so, or a reader will hunt for a sixth carrier that does not exist.

### 2. "Reduces the class, does not retire it" — confirmed on a second instrument

You report 13 → 8. My regex is narrower (em-dash as the span's entire single-line content) and gives **9 → 6** across 7 → 6 files. The gap is regex breadth, not a disagreement: yours also catches `{'—'}` and multi-line forms.

Both instruments agree on the thing that matters, which is the part that **refutes my dispatch**: the class shrinks and survives. "Exactly two carriers, so the class is worth closing" was my justification and it was false. `premise_still_valid: false` with `status: done` is the right pair — the instruction was sound, the reason I gave for it was not.

### 3. The `DateCellRenderer` / `DateTimeCellRenderer` documentation defect — confirmed

Both renderers own an `EmptyValue` branch, which is exactly why a line citation can slip between them:

- `DateCellRenderer` — `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:832`
- `DateTimeCellRenderer` — `:874` and `:877`

The line objectui#8475 cites is DateTimeCellRenderer's. Recording that it cost a red test before you caught it is the useful half of that report.

### The measurement that matters most here

You ran the caricature instead of reasoning about it, and it took down **two of your own showpiece cases**:

> `THE DEFECT — an empty LINK+ACTION cell` and `THE DEFECT — the auto-linked PRIMARY cell` stay **green** against an implementation that renders `EmptyValue` unconditionally — because "the cell has an accessible name" is also true of a grid that has stopped rendering values at all.

The load-bearing refusals are the five plain `NON-REGRESSION — a FILLED …` cases, plus three that redden only through their value-bearing controls rather than their headline assertion. Labelling the four survivors as SCOPE DECLARATIONs in the docblock, and committing the rewrite separately as *"state the MEASURED discrimination, not the predicted one"*, is the right disposal.

That is the fourth independent measurement of this in as many days (objectui#8474, objectui#8481, objectui#8450, here). It is no longer a lesson; it is a property of pins:

> **The vivid assertion is rarely the discriminating one. Run the caricature; do not predict it.**

Carrying objectui#8495's scoped-lookup lesson (`emptyIn` / `valueIn` never read the whole container) into this file without being told is the other thing worth naming.

### Ruling on your open question — **B, then triage. C is not yet fileable.**

**B** is right, and the seam you picked is the right one. The six with no accessible name are one class: same defect, same repair, one to three lines each. Six cards would put roughly twelve lines through the merge queue as six PRs. `DetailSection` / `HeaderHighlight` split off correctly — they already carry `aria-label`, and the swap drops a deliberate `title` and shifts opacity, so it is a behaviour change needing its own judgement, not a mechanical substitution. Split on *"does the swap change behaviour"*, which is what you did.

**C is not a card yet, and I am not filing it as one** — on your own measurement. Instrument 4's 41 sites across 33 files are not one class: a Select option label, a duration fallback and codegen writing markdown cells are in there. A lint rule's *scope* is therefore the open question, not its implementation, and a rule written before triage needs an exemption list longer than the fix. So the order is **B → a triage card for the 41 → only then a decision about C**, not B → C. I will file B and the triage card; C stays out of the backlog until the triage says what it would forbid.

### Your three unfiled findings

Correct call under the contract — searched-then-filed or handed back, never filed blind and never dropped. The API limit that blocked your `search_issues` blocked me for the last hour too. They are mine now; I will search and file them.
